reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
reviews.body:
## Pull request overview This PR modernizes BatMon’s beta UX by introducing a new “layout + theme” system (including custom JSON themes + editor UI), refreshing the menu bar dropdown UI across multiple layouts, and polishing settings/reconnect/forget flows (plus some widget-sync plumbing). **Changes:** - Adds a theme registry + custom theme loading/editing pipeline, and exposes layout/theme selection in Settings with live previews. - Redesigns the menu bar dropdown into multiple layouts (native/rich/minimal/tui) and expands display customization (compact mode, separators, experimental formats, disconnected icon theming). - Improves reconnect/forget behavior and updates persistence/versioning/build metadata (also introduces WidgetKit timeline reload hooks and app-group defaults usage). ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 32 out of 34 changed files in this pull request and generated 10 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | bat-mon-PRD.md | Adds product requirements doc for the app (MVP goals, UX, technical strategy). | | README.md | Adds beta-focused user documentation, theme JSON format, and troubleshooting. | | LICENSE | Adds MIT license text. | | BATMON_PROJECT_PLAN.md | Adds a comprehensive planning/architecture document. | | BatMon/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift | Adds Appearance tab (layout/theme selection, theme editor), revamps Display settings UI (compact mode, separators, experimental formats, disconnected icon customization), and copy tweaks. | | BatMon/Views/Settings/SFSymbolPicker.swift | Adds a curated SF Symbols picker sheet for compact mode custom icons. | | BatMon/Views/MenuBar/MenuBarView.swift | Refactors dropdown UI into multiple layouts (native/rich/minimal/tui) with theme support and improved reconnect/permission UX. | | BatMon/Views/MenuBar/BatIconView.swift | Adds a custom bat-shaped disconnected icon with optional border. | | BatMon/Utilities/LaunchAtLogin.swift | Introduces ServiceManagement-based launch-at-login helper. | | BatMon/Utilities/Constants.swift | Updates app metadata/version sourcing, adds app group identifier and widget-related UserDefaults keys. | | BatMon/Theme/Themes/SystemTheme.swift | Adds “System” theme implementation. | | BatMon/Theme/Themes/GruvboxTheme.swift | Adds Gruvbox dark theme. | | BatMon/Theme/Themes/GruvboxLightTheme.swift | Adds Gruvbox light theme. | | BatMon/Theme/Themes/TokyoNightTheme.swift | Adds Tokyo Night theme. | | BatMon/Theme/Themes/SolarizedLightTheme.swift | Adds Solarized Light theme. | | BatMon/Theme/ThemeRegistry.swift | Adds central theme registry (hardcoded + custom themes). | | BatMon/Theme/ThemeEnvironment.swift | Adds SwiftUI Environment key for the active theme. | | BatMon/Theme/MenuLayout.swift | Adds menu dropdown layout enum (native/rich/minimal/tui). | | BatMon/Theme/CustomThemeLoader.swift | Adds themes.json loading/saving/validation and file watching. | | BatMon/Theme/ConfigurableTheme.swift | Adds configurable theme model + validation and JSON import/export helpers. | | BatMon/Theme/ColorTheme.swift | Adds ColorTheme protocol + battery-color derivation. | | BatMon/Resources/Info.plist | Switches to MARKETING_VERSION/CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION placeholders. | | BatMon/Resources/Assets.xcassets/Contents.json | Adds asset catalog manifest. | | BatMon/Resources/Assets.xcassets/MenuBarIcon.imageset/Contents.json | Adds imageset manifest for menu bar icon. | | BatMon/Resources/Assets.xcassets/MenuBarIcon.imageset/bat-icon.svg | Adds/updates vector bat icon source asset. | | BatMon/Resources/Assets.xcassets/MenuBarIcon.imageset/bat-icon.pdf | Adds/updates PDF vector bat icon asset. | | BatMon/Models/ConnectionState.swift | Adds a helper to detect “Bluetooth unavailable” state (currently via message string). | | BatMon/Models/BatteryLevel.swift | Removes unused fields/helpers from BatteryLevel. | | BatMon/Models/AppSettings.swift | Introduces layout/theme/compact/experimental settings, disconnected icon customization, and migration from legacy MenuStyle. | | BatMon/Managers/PreferencesManager.swift | Moves defaults to app-group suite when available, performs MenuStyle migration, and syncs some settings to widget keys. | | BatMon/Managers/BluetoothManager.swift | Improves scanning behavior, caching for reconnect, adds forgetSelectedKeyboard, clamps battery % values, and writes widget snapshot + reload calls. | | BatMon/App/BatMonApp.swift | Initializes default themes, updates MenuBarExtra label rendering (including custom disconnected icon rendering), and refreshes label on relevant settings changes. | | BatMon/App/AppDelegate.swift | Switches notification permission error reporting to os.Logger and avoids strong capture. | | BatMon.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj | Wires new files/resources into the project and bumps macOS deployment target to 14.0. |

**Actionable comments posted: 14**
🤖 Fix all issues with AI agents ``` In `@BATMON_PROJECT_PLAN.md`: - Around line 1720-1727: Update the placeholder constants inside enum AppInfo: replace bundleIdentifier value "com.yourdomain.bat-mon" with "com.paolo.bat-mon" and update githubURL and issuesURL to use the correct GitHub owner by replacing "yourusername" with "PapaniaP" (e.g. "https://github.com/PapaniaP/bat-mon" and "https://github.com/PapaniaP/bat-mon/issues"); ensure appName, version, and buildNumber remain correct and propagate these updated values wherever AppInfo.githubURL or AppInfo.issuesURL are referenced. - Around line 1470-1472: The LSMinimumSystemVersion entry currently set to "13.0" conflicts with the project's stated macOS requirement; update the LSMinimumSystemVersion key value from "13.0" to "14.0" so it matches the README, badge, and PRD; locate the LSMinimumSystemVersion / 13.0 pair in BATMON_PROJECT_PLAN.md and change the string to "14.0". In `@BatMon/App/BatMonApp.swift`: - Around line 49-52: When rendering the compact-mode icon in BatMonApp (inside the compactMode branch), guard against an empty customCompactIcon: if settings.compactIcon == .custom and settings.customCompactIcon is empty or whitespace, fall back to a safe default SF symbol name (e.g., the standard battery icon) instead of passing "" to Image(systemName:); update the logic that computes iconName (used by Image(systemName:)) to choose settings.customCompactIcon only when it is non-empty, otherwise use the default symbol. In `@BatMon/Managers/BluetoothManager.swift`: - Around line 206-225: forgetSelectedKeyboard() currently doesn't stop the polling timer, leaving the poller alive until didDisconnectPeripheral runs; update forgetSelectedKeyboard() to explicitly call stopPolling() (same call used in disconnect()) before nil-ing connectedPeripheral and clearing state so the polling timer is stopped immediately and consistent with refreshBatteryLevels() guards and the existing disconnect() behavior. In `@BatMon/Theme/CustomThemeLoader.swift`: - Around line 158-188: The watcher created in startWatching(...) doesn't recreate itself after the watched file is deleted/renamed; update the dispatchSource.setEventHandler to inspect dispatchSource?.data for .delete or .rename, and when those flags are present call stopWatching() and then re-establish the watch by calling startWatching(onChange) (use a weak self capture and optionally a short async delay to allow the file to be recreated), while preserving the existing onChange invocation for .write events; ensure fileDescriptor and dispatchSource are cleaned up in setCancelHandler and stopWatching so the re-created watcher opens a fresh file descriptor. - Around line 5-6: The class-level doc comment for CustomThemeLoader incorrectly states the themes file is at ~/.config/bat-mon/themes.json; update the comment to reflect the actual resolved path (~/Library/Application Support/BatMon/themes.json) or, better, describe that the loader stores themes in the user's Application Support directory on macOS. Locate the path-resolving code or property inside CustomThemeLoader (e.g., the method or property that computes the themes file URL/path) and change the comment to mention the platform-specific location or note that the loader uses the user's Application Support directory rather than ~/.config. In `@BatMon/Theme/Themes/GruvboxTheme.swift`: - Line 10: The background Color in GruvboxTheme.swift (the var background) uses RGB values that don't match the commented hex `#282828`; update the value to the accurate sRGB equivalent (40/255 ≈ 0.157) so the color matches the Gruvbox spec (e.g., set red/green/blue to ~0.157) or alternatively construct the Color from the hex/255 components to ensure exact fidelity to `#282828`. - Around line 23-26: The static color properties aqua, blue, and purple in GruvboxTheme (static let aqua, blue, purple) are unused; either remove these dead properties from GruvboxTheme.swift or retain them with a short explanatory comment indicating they are reserved for future use (e.g., "Reserved for future theme variants — do not remove") so their presence is intentional and documented. In `@BatMon/Views/MenuBar/MenuBarView.swift`: - Around line 1251-1281: MinimalActionPill declares a PillStyle and a style property but never uses it, so both .primary and .secondary render the same; update MinimalActionPill (and its PillStyle enum) to switch visual values (foregroundStyle and background color/opacity) based on style (e.g., use theme.accent for .primary and theme.secondaryAccent or a subdued theme.text/color for .secondary with different opacities) by replacing the hardcoded theme.accent usages in body with a conditional (switch or ternary) keyed on style, or if you intentionally don't need two styles remove the style property and PillStyle enum entirely to avoid an unused parameter. - Around line 760-762: The nested enum named ButtonStyle inside MenuBarView (used by RichPillButton) shadows SwiftUI's ButtonStyle protocol; rename the enum (for example to PillButtonStyle or Style) and update all references (e.g., the enum declaration and any properties or initializers on RichPillButton that use ButtonStyle) so RichPillButton now uses the new name to avoid protocol shadowing and potential compiler confusion. In `@BatMon/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift`: - Around line 756-769: In deleteTheme(), avoid changing preferencesManager.settings.colorThemeId to "system" before deletion; instead call themeRegistry.removeCustomTheme(withId: theme.id) first and only update preferencesManager.settings.colorThemeId (to "system") after the removeCustomTheme call succeeds (before calling dismiss()), so any thrown error leaves the original selection intact; keep the existing catch branch that sets errorMessage and ensure you still call dismiss() only on success. - Around line 729-754: The saveTheme() flow creates a new ConfigurableTheme whose id is regenerated from the new name, so CustomThemeLoader.updateTheme (and themeRegistry.saveCustomTheme) can't find the original entry and a duplicate is appended; to fix it preserve the original theme id when renaming by carrying the old id into the update flow: when editing an existing theme (detect via preferencesManager.settings.colorThemeId or the editor's originalTheme reference), set the new ConfigurableTheme's id to the original id before calling themeRegistry.saveCustomTheme (or change saveCustomTheme/updateTheme to accept an optional originalId and use that to locate and replace the existing JSON entry), ensuring CustomThemeLoader.updateTheme still searches by the original id rather than the regenerated one. In `@README.md`: - Around line 78-82: Docs use two different bundle identifier strings — "com.paolo.bat-mon" and "com.yourdomain.bat-mon" — causing inconsistency; pick a single canonical identifier (either the real bundle id "com.paolo.bat-mon" or the placeholder "com.yourdomain.bat-mon") and update all docs to match (specifically replace occurrences of "com.paolo.bat-mon" and "com.yourdomain.bat-mon" so README.md, BATMON_PROJECT_PLAN.md, and bat-mon-PRD.md are consistent), and add a short clarifying note where appropriate indicating whether the identifier shown is an example/placeholder or the actual app bundle id. - Around line 7-8: The License badge in README.md points to /blob/main/LICENSE which 404s because the repo default branch is master; update the license badge URL to reference /blob/master/LICENSE (replace "main" with "master") so the link resolves correctly, and verify the markdown line containing the License badge is updated accordingly. ```
🧹 Nitpick comments (18)
BatMon/Views/Settings/SFSymbolPicker.swift (1)
`73-78`: **No empty state when search yields zero results.** When `filteredSymbols` is empty, the user sees a blank scroll area with no feedback. Consider adding a brief "No matching symbols" message.
Proposed fix ```diff // Grid ScrollView { + if filteredSymbols.isEmpty { + Text("No matching symbols") + .foregroundStyle(.secondary) + .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity) + .padding(.top, 40) + } LazyVGrid(columns: [GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: 50))], spacing: 12) { ```
BatMon.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj (1)
`159-165`: **Empty groups may be leftover scaffolding.** `GRP005` (ViewModels), `GRP006C` (KeyboardSelection), and `GRP006D` (Setup) are all empty groups. If these are intentional placeholders for future development, that's fine. Otherwise, consider removing them to reduce project clutter. Also applies to: 195-208
BatMon/Models/ConnectionState.swift (1)
`38-43`: **String-based Bluetooth detection is fragile.** Matching on `message.lowercased().contains("bluetooth")` ties this logic to the exact wording of error messages. If the message text changes or is localized, this will silently break. Consider using a dedicated enum case (e.g., `.bluetoothUnavailable`) or a structured error type instead of relying on string content. That said, for a beta this is workable — just keep in mind it's a maintenance risk.
♻️ Suggested approach using a dedicated enum case ```diff enum ConnectionState: Equatable { case disconnected case searching case connecting case connected case reconnecting(attempt: Int, maxAttempts: Int) case failed(String) + case bluetoothUnavailable var isBluetoothUnavailable: Bool { - if case .failed(let message) = self { - return message.lowercased().contains("bluetooth") - } - return false + if case .bluetoothUnavailable = self { return true } + return false } ```
BatMon/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift (1)
`100-233`: **Consider splitting this file — it contains 18+ views (~1250 lines).** This single file houses the entire settings UI (SettingsView, GeneralSettingsView, AppearanceSettingsView, all preview mini views, card views, ThemeEditorSheet, DisplaySettingsView, NotificationSettingsView, KeyboardsSettingsView, AboutView). Extracting the appearance-related views (preview minis, cards, theme editor) into separate files would improve navigability.
BatMon/Managers/PreferencesManager.swift (2)
`17-17`: **Silent fallback to `.standard` if app group is misconfigured.** If `UserDefaults(suiteName:)` returns `nil` (e.g., the app group entitlement is missing or the identifier doesn't match), the fallback to `.standard` means the app works fine but widgets will never see updated data — since they'll read from the shared suite while the app writes to `.standard`. Consider logging a warning when the suite initializer fails so this doesn't become a silent debugging headache.
♻️ Suggested improvement ```diff - private let defaults = UserDefaults(suiteName: AppInfo.appGroupIdentifier) ?? .standard + private let defaults: UserDefaults = { + if let shared = UserDefaults(suiteName: AppInfo.appGroupIdentifier) { + return shared + } + Logger(subsystem: AppInfo.bundleIdentifier, category: "Preferences") + .error("Failed to create UserDefaults for app group '\(AppInfo.appGroupIdentifier)' — falling back to .standard. Widgets will not receive updates.") + return .standard + }() ```
--- `32-34`: **Unconditional `saveSettings()` on every init triggers widget timeline reload even when no migration occurred.** `saveSettings()` calls `WidgetCenter.shared.reloadAllTimelines()`, so every app launch reloads widget timelines regardless of whether anything changed. Consider gating this on whether migration actually ran:
♻️ Suggested improvement ```diff - self.hasCompletedSetup = defaults.bool(forKey: UserDefaultsKeys.hasCompletedSetup) - - // Save settings after migration (if any occurred) - saveSettings() + self.hasCompletedSetup = defaults.bool(forKey: UserDefaultsKeys.hasCompletedSetup) + + // Save settings only if migration actually occurred + if loaded.menuStyle != nil { // nil means migration ran and cleared it + // Note: by this point loaded.menuStyle was set to nil by migrateFromMenuStyleIfNeeded() + // so we need a different signal — e.g., a flag from the migration method + } ```
One approach: have `migrateFromMenuStyleIfNeeded()` return a `Bool` indicating whether migration occurred, and only call `saveSettings()` when `true`.
BatMon/Theme/MenuLayout.swift (1)
`21-28`: **Nit: `description` property name shadows the standard `CustomStringConvertible.description`.** While there's no conformance conflict, using `description` as a property name on a Swift type can cause confusion when debugging (e.g., `print(layout)` won't use this). A name like `subtitle` or `summary` would be less ambiguous.
BatMon/App/BatMonApp.swift (1)
`22-24`: **Consider extracting the `.id()` key into a computed property.** This concatenated string is long and fragile — every new setting that affects the label must be manually appended. A computed `var menuBarIdentityKey: String` on `AppSettings` (or a `Hashable`-conforming struct of the relevant fields) would be easier to maintain and less error-prone.
♻️ Example approach Add a computed property on `AppSettings`: ```swift var menuBarIdentityKey: String { "\(displayFormat.rawValue)-\(compactMode)-\(compactIcon.rawValue)-\(customCompactIcon)-\(useExperimentalFormat)-\(experimentalFormat.rawValue)-\(colorThemeId)-\(useThemeDisconnectedIconColors ?? true)-\(disconnectedIconFillHex)-\(disconnectedIconBorderEnabled)-\(disconnectedIconBorderHex)" } ``` Then in `BatMonApp`: ```diff - .id( - "menubar-\(preferencesManager.settings.displayFormat.rawValue)-..." - ) + .id("menubar-\(preferencesManager.settings.menuBarIdentityKey)") ```
BatMon/Theme/Themes/TokyoNightTheme.swift (1)
`9-24`: **Inconsistent color initializer compared to sibling themes.** `GruvboxLightTheme` and `SolarizedLightTheme` use `Color(hex:)`, while this file uses `Color(red:green:blue:)`. The float values introduce rounding drift from the hex values in the comments (e.g., `0.11` → `0x1C`, but the comment says `#1a1b26` → `0x1B`). Consider using `Color(hex:)` for consistency and exact palette fidelity.
♻️ Example for the first few lines ```diff - var background: Color { Color(red: 0.10, green: 0.11, blue: 0.15) } // `#1a1b26` - var backgroundSecondary: Color { Color(red: 0.14, green: 0.15, blue: 0.20) } // `#24283b` + var background: Color { Color(hex: "#1a1b26") } // storm bg + var backgroundSecondary: Color { Color(hex: "#24283b") } // storm bg secondary ```
BatMon/Theme/ConfigurableTheme.swift (1)
`79-79`: **Theme ID generation is duplicated across `ConfigurableTheme` and `CustomThemeLoader`.** The `name.lowercased().replacingOccurrences(of: " ", with: "_")` logic appears in `parse(from:)` (line 79), `init(name:...)` (line 138), and `CustomThemeLoader.themeId(from:)` (lines 98-101 in CustomThemeLoader.swift). If the normalization rule ever changes, all three sites must be updated in lockstep.
♻️ Centralise ID derivation ```swift // e.g., in ConfigurableTheme or a shared utility static func deriveId(from name: String) -> String { name.lowercased().replacingOccurrences(of: " ", with: "_") } ``` Then use `ConfigurableTheme.deriveId(from: name)` everywhere.
Also applies to: 138-138
BatMon/Theme/CustomThemeLoader.swift (2)
`6-7`: **Singleton `init` is not `private`, allowing unintended additional instances.**
Proposed fix ```diff class CustomThemeLoader { static let shared = CustomThemeLoader() + private init() {} ```
--- `98-102`: **ID derivation logic is duplicated from `ConfigurableTheme.parse`.** Both `themeId(from:)` here and `ConfigurableTheme.parse(from:)` derive the ID as `name.lowercased().replacingOccurrences(of: " ", with: "_")`. If one changes, the other won't, causing silent mismatches in `addTheme`/`updateTheme`/`removeTheme`. Consider extracting a shared static helper or reusing the parse result's ID.
BatMon/Models/AppSettings.swift (2)
`281-289`: **`toHex()` may silently return `"#000000"` for non-RGB colors (e.g., grayscale or catalog colors).** `NSColor(self).cgColor.components` can have fewer than 3 elements for grayscale colors. Consider converting to a known RGB color space first:
Suggested improvement ```diff func toHex() -> String { - guard let components = NSColor(self).cgColor.components, components.count >= 3 else { + guard let rgbColor = NSColor(self).usingColorSpace(.sRGB), + let components = rgbColor.cgColor.components, components.count >= 3 else { return "#000000" } ```
--- `256-279`: **`Color(hex:)` silently defaults to black for unrecognized hex lengths.** Lengths like 4, 5, or 7 characters (after stripping non-alphanumerics) will silently produce black. This is a reasonable fallback, but worth noting that malformed hex strings won't surface any warning to the user or developer. Consider logging a warning for unexpected lengths, especially since theme JSON is user-editable.
BatMon/Views/MenuBar/MenuBarView.swift (4)
`6-11`: **`openBluetoothSettings()` is a free (global) function — consider scoping it.** A module-level free function pollutes the namespace. Consider making it a `static` method on a helper type or a private extension, especially since it's called from multiple view structs. --- `889-903`: **`timeAgoDisplay()` doesn't handle future dates or very large intervals.** If `self` is in the future, `seconds` will be negative, producing incorrect output (e.g., a large negative number of hours). Consider clamping or returning a fallback for non-positive intervals. Also, intervals beyond 24 hours will show e.g., "48h ago" — you may want a day-level fallback.
Suggested improvement ```diff func timeAgoDisplay() -> String { let seconds = Int(-self.timeIntervalSinceNow) + guard seconds >= 0 else { return "just now" } + if seconds < 60 { return "just now" } else if seconds < 3600 { let minutes = seconds / 60 return "\(minutes)m ago" - } else { + } else if seconds < 86400 { let hours = seconds / 3600 return "\(hours)h ago" + } else { + let days = seconds / 86400 + return "\(days)d ago" } } ```
--- `1-1599`: **This ~1600-line file contains four complete menu style implementations — consider splitting into separate files.** Each style (Native, Rich, Minimal, TUI) is self-contained with its own set of subviews. Splitting into `NativeMenuBarView.swift`, `RichMenuBarView.swift`, `MinimalMenuBarView.swift`, and `TUIMenuBarView.swift` would significantly improve navigability and reduce merge conflicts. --- `1332-1371`: **`FlowLayout` is unused.** Consider removing it per YAGNI, or add a comment clarifying which feature will use it (the MARK comment mentions "wrapping keyboard pills" but no code currently implements this).

**Actionable comments posted: 1**
🤖 Fix all issues with AI agents ``` In `@BatMon/Theme/ThemeRegistry.swift`: - Around line 36-38: The file-watcher callback passed to CustomThemeLoader.shared.startWatching may be invoked off the main thread, and calling reloadCustomThemes() can mutate `@Published` properties (customThemes, invalidThemes) from a background thread; ensure the callback dispatches to the main queue before calling reloadCustomThemes (e.g., wrap the closure body in a DispatchQueue.main.async { [weak self] in self?.reloadCustomThemes() } or move the main-thread hop into reloadCustomThemes) so all ObservableObject/@Published updates occur on the main thread. ```
🧹 Nitpick comments (2)
BatMon/Theme/ThemeRegistry.swift (2)
`41-43`: **`deinit` is unreachable — singleton held by `static let` is never deallocated.** Since `shared` is a `static let`, this `deinit` is dead code; `stopWatching()` will never execute. If the intent is cleanup on app termination, consider calling `stopWatching()` explicitly from an app-lifecycle hook (e.g., `applicationWillTerminate`). Otherwise, removing `deinit` avoids giving the false impression that the watcher is cleaned up. --- `76-80`: **`removeCustomTheme` silently ignores attempts to remove a hardcoded theme.** Consider throwing an error or returning a `Bool` so callers can distinguish "not found / not removable" from success. Currently, calling `removeCustomTheme(withId: "system")` succeeds silently, which could mask bugs at the call site.
